summary: Read ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md and story 1-1 and found the six shared contracts the contracts package must define in src/contracts/, which imports nothing else from src/: (1) the AD-5 event envelope with eight fields (ts, seq, feature, run, step, emitter, type, payload), an open list of event types, and passthrough of parent_tool_use_id and session_id; (2) the AD-3 Command enum covering the 14 steering controls; (3) the AD-25 question contract with asked/resolved/deflected states and resolver and principal fields; (4) the AD-35 error shape {code, message, retryable, cause} with its disposition table, where unknown codes fall back to abandon-and-hand-off; (5) the AD-28 schema_version field and a helper that refuses unrecognised versions; (6) the typed step input/output envelope. They share one contract registry keyed by id, and it exports draft-7 JSON Schema through a single toJsonSchema helper. Every step contract must stay inside the structured-outputs subset.
provenance: analysis: docs/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-agent-orcastrator-2026-09-19/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md (AD-2, AD-3, AD-5, AD-17, AD-19, AD-25, AD-28, AD-31, AD-35; Structural Seed)
analysis: docs/specs/spec-agent-orchestrator/interface-contract.md (steering controls the Command enum must cover)

decisions.question: Should the six contracts be separate modules, or one combined schema file?
decisions.answer: One module per contract under src/contracts/ (event.ts, command.ts, question.ts, error.ts, schema-version.ts, step.ts). registry.ts maps contract id to Zod schema and is the only place z.toJSONSchema is called, always with target draft-7.
decisions.rationale: AD-17 agent TOML refers to contracts by id and never inlines a schema. Zod 4 defaults to draft-2020-12, which claude -p --json-schema rejects. If export goes through one helper, a call site cannot forget the draft-7 argument, and the subset guard and round-trip suites can iterate over a single registry.

artifacts.description: Full session transcript of the analysis step: the spine and story 1-1 reads and the reasoning that identified the six shared contracts (evidence plane, read on demand).

questions.prompt: Should the command intent file schema (AD-19: the durable file under runs/<run-id>/commands/ that carries a Command, its arguments and its principal) be defined in this story, or deferred to the story that builds the reconciler or renderers?
questions.brief: Story 1-1 defines the AD-3 Command enum. It does not list a schema for the intent file that wraps the enum. AD-19 makes that file the only thing the reconciler consumes, and it must record a principal. Both renderers and the engine will depend on it, which suggests it belongs in contracts. Adding it here grows a story that is already flagged oversized.

options.label: Define the command intent schema in this story
options.consequence: Adds src/contracts/command-intent.ts and a registry entry. Both renderers and the reconciler build against one shape from the start. The story grows by one file and roughly two matrix rows.

options.label: Defer it to the reconciler/renderer stories
options.consequence: Keeps 1-1 within its current scope. The first consumer defines the schema later and must place it in src/contracts/, with some risk that the two renderers drift in the meantime.

options.label: Add a minimal envelope now and fill in the per-command payloads later
options.consequence: Fixes command, principal, ts and schema_version now and leaves payload open. This limits drift at little cost, but a later story has to tighten the payloads.

escape.label: Pause and ask the spec author
escape.consequence: Planning for contracts-package waits until the story's scope is clarified.

questions.default_action: Proceed with the minimal command intent envelope (option 'stub') and record the choice in the story's Spec Change Log.
